newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence to rise more - Conference Bd.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence to rise more - Conference Bd.

text.p: The Conference Board, a leading business research and membership network, said consumer confidence in the U.S. -- already at a 28-year high -- could rise further.
Ken Golstein, senior economist at The Conference Board told Reuters Financial Television that any further bolstering of consumer attitudes depends on the unemployment rate.
"If we're going still lower on the unemployment rate, there is indeed at least a chance that we'll go still higher on consumer confidence," he said.
Goldstein said he expected the unemployment rate to fall further, perhaps to 4.5 percent from its current 4.8 percent.
Indeed, he added that current consumer confidence levels indicate consumers, too, expect employment conditions to remain firm. "Consumer don't expect the labor market to drop off," he said.

The Conference Board's June index of consumer confidence rocketed to 129.6 from a revised reading of 127.9 in May. The 129.6 level marks the highest reading for U.S. consumer confidence since August of 1969 when it stood at 131.7.
Turning to inflation, Goldstein said prices in the U.S. were not completely under control, adding that he expected an uptick in inflation down the road.
"This is going to drive up the price of labor and eventually this strong demand will also drive up the price of materials, so inflation is going higher," he said.

As for Federal Reserve policy, the Conference Board economist said the central bank could ratchet up interest rates by 50 basis points if the long bond yield tops 7.25 percent. By the end of the year, Goldstein said long bond yields should push to 7.20 percent.
